nativeWindow constructor stores native_window_swap at drawable+0x10 (0x31becec4); present callback verified from literal 0x304 at 0x31becfa8.

CopyImageInfo entry r0 is the shared queue handle, r1/r2 time double bits. At its epilogue r0 is a boolean. Selected-serial point observes r0 serial before storing to output+4 at r1; a later boolean return is still required.

Render queue entry r0 is this. At generation cmp (0x31b92794), r0=this, r1=update object, r2=cached generation, r3=update generation. The equal branch bypasses the queue query. Both generation values are loaded before this point.
Render image serial point is before cmp r1,r3: r1=selected serial, r3=previous serial. A reached comparison does not prove the image is changed because a timestamp equality comparison follows.

Producer and consumer shared queue addresses belong to different processes. Equal numeric pointers are not queue identity; serial equality and ordered surface association alone are not independent shared-memory proof.
SwapWait, native buffer acquisition and descriptor-absent points removed to stay within the 32 point limit. Scheduling and nonnull unlock observations retained.

Insert base-serial point precedes str r3 to slot+0x24; r3 came from shared queue+0xc. Later 0x31b84140 increments the slot serial if flags&6. The pinned native caller selects 0x10002/0x10003, optionally OR 0x10/0x1, so bit1 is always set. For a successful nested insert from that callsite, predicted published serial is base+1 modulo32bits. This is static control-flow derivation, not a direct post-increment snapshot; preserve the observed base and the derivation.
AAC ProduceOutputPackets entry 0x303ddb34 and sole normal epilogue 0x303ddd08 were checked against the matching cache disassembly. Exception/throw exits are not normal returns and remain unmatched.

convertScaledFloatToS16 entry 0x303f4d98 and sole epilogue 0x303f4f44 were checked against matching disassembly. It returns void: epilogue r0 is not a success result. Entry r0=input, r1=output, r2=scale float bits, r3=scalar count; output alignment comes from entry r1.

Audio boundaries pair within the same guest thread. Selected-thread running time includes guest kernel/native execution while that thread is selected; it is not a count of instructions in this function alone.

Four CA transaction observations and two shared-queue update observations are removed from the queue manifest; producer insertion, queue selection, render generation/serial, framebuffer mapping and guest scheduling observations remain. Thirty points total. No audio arithmetic or alignment-fault instrumentation is needed.
